transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. [Name], I'm here because... well, I've just been avoiding my own workshop for a while now. And I also stay away from any family get-togethers if there's a chance my brother-in-law is going to be there. I guess I'm just tired of constantly having to plan my whole life around avoiding things that remind me of... well, of what happened. It's just getting to be too much work.
You mentioned 'what happened' — can you tell me what specific event you're referring to?

Well, to be honest with you, I'd really rather not get into the exact details of it today. It was just... a bad situation that happened a while back. I know I'm here to get help, and I probably need to talk about it eventually, but... spelling out the whole story right now is just not something I'm ready to do. I just call it 'what happened' so I don't have to think about the specifics.
When you think about avoiding your workshop and family gatherings, do you experience sudden physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or difficulty breathing?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My heart doesn't race, and I don't get sweaty or out of breath. It's not really a physical thing for me... I just know I don't want to be anywhere near those situations, so I stay away. But no, I don't get those physical symptoms you're talking about.
When you think about going to your workshop or being around your brother-in-law, what specifically are you afraid might happen or what are you worried about?

Well, I'm not really afraid that something specific is going to happen, exactly. It's more just... I don't want to be reminded of it. If I go out to the workshop, or if I see him, it just brings everything back up in my mind. I'm not worried about getting hurt or anything like that now. I just... I just don't want to think about it. So it's easier to just avoid it altogether.
Over the past few weeks or months, how has your overall mood been? Have you been feeling down, sad, or depressed most of the time?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad or depressed. My mood has been mostly fine, really. I mean, I have my days like anyone else, but I'm not walking around feeling down all the time. I just... I prefer to keep to myself a bit more lately, I guess. But no, overall, I don't feel depressed.

When you say that being in the workshop or seeing your brother-in-law brings everything back up in your mind, do you mean that unwanted memories or images of what happened suddenly pop into your head, even when you're not trying to think about it?

Yeah, that's exactly what I mean. It just happens out of nowhere. I could be doing something completely normal, like... well, like shaving in the morning, or just working on a painting in the house. And then, suddenly, I'll just see his hand with that heavy tool again. 

It's like a picture that just pops right into my head when I'm not even trying to think about it. And when I see it... well, it still makes my chest tighten up.
When you see that image of his hand with the tool pop into your head, besides your chest tightening, do you feel a strong emotional reaction like fear, anger, or panic in that moment?

No, I wouldn't say I feel panic or anger... not really. It's mostly just that physical feeling, like I said, with my chest getting tight. I don't feel terrified or anything like that. I just see the picture, my chest tightens up a bit, and I just try to push it right back out of my mind. But no, I don't have a big emotional reaction like you're describing.
How long ago did this event with your brother-in-law happen? Was it within the past month, or longer ago than that?

Well, it's definitely been longer than a month. This whole thing... it started right after that confrontation with my brother-in-law. That was about two years and four months ago, roughly. So yeah, it's been going on since then.

When you see that image of his hand with the tool pop into your head, do you ever feel emotionally numb or disconnected from what's happening around you, like you're watching things from a distance or like things aren't quite real?

No, I don't think so. I don't feel numb or disconnected like you're saying. It's just that image popping into my head and my chest getting a bit tight. I still feel normal otherwise, and I know where I am and what's going on around me. I don't feel like I'm watching from a distance or anything like that.
When that image pops into your head and your chest tightens, do you find it hard to remember other details about what happened, or does your mind go blank about parts of that event?

Well, I remember the shouting, and seeing that tool plain enough. But... yeah, I guess there is a part I can't quite pull up. There's a blank spot right around how the whole thing actually ended. It's just like somebody cut a few minutes right out of the story. I don't really know what happened right at the end there.

When that image of his hand with the tool pops into your head and your chest gets tight, do you ever lose track of time, or does it feel like you're reliving the moment rather than just remembering it?

No, I don't think I lose track of time. I always know where I am when it happens. It's... well, it's really just a memory. A strong picture in my head, sure, but I don't feel like I'm actually back there living it all over again. I just remember it.

When that image pops into your head and your chest tightens, how much does it bother you or interfere with what you're trying to do at that moment — is it just a minor annoyance, or does it significantly disrupt your day?

Well, it bothers me a little, I suppose. But I wouldn't say it disrupts my whole day. It's more like a... a minor annoyance. I just take a breath, let the tightness pass, and go back to whatever I was doing. It doesn't stop me in my tracks or anything like that.

If you think about your life right now, would you say that most of your difficulties — the avoidance, staying away from your workshop and family — are they still mainly connected to what happened with your brother-in-law, or have other things become more of a problem for you over time?

Well, I'd say it's still mostly just connected to what happened with him. I mean... I haven't really noticed anything else becoming a big problem for me. It all pretty much just goes back to that day. I don't really have a lot of other things getting in the way, just... just staying out of the shop and keeping my distance sometimes because of that.

When that image pops into your head and your chest tightens, do you ever feel like your body isn't responding the way you want it to, or do you feel disconnected from your own body or actions in that moment?

No, I don't think so. I mean, my chest gets tight, sure, but I don't feel disconnected or anything like that. I'm still just me, sitting there. My body does what I want it to do, I just... I just have that tight feeling for a minute. But I don't feel like I'm outside myself or anything strange like that.
Besides that specific image of his hand with the tool, do you have other unwanted memories or thoughts about what happened that day that pop into your head unexpectedly?

No, it's really just that one specific thing. Out of nowhere, I'll just see his hand holding that heavy tool again. It's like a picture that just pops into my head, completely uninvited. It happens when I'm doing normal things, like shaving or working on a painting. And like I said, when I see it, it still makes my chest tighten up. But it's just that one image, nothing else really comes back to me like that.
